title: Eventual kernel vanishing for principal puncture restriction
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of depth at least three [def-weil-pbc-depth], let g lie in its maximal ideal, and let W be its punctured spectrum [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put f:R to R/(g), I=ker(f) and W_n=openThickening f W n [lem-sbc-finite-etale-adic-sections-transfer]. For each n there is m at least n such that any two scalars a,b in R with the same canonical image in Gamma(W_m,O) satisfy a-b in I^(n+1). Thus the kernel of R/I^(m+1) to Gamma(W_m,O) maps to zero in R/I^(n+1). No injectivity of an individual finite-level restriction is asserted.

source.place: Tags 0H3E (Example 20.39.3, pro-isomorphism of the two-term cones with ordinary quotients), 0BLD (degree zero), 0BK0 and 0AVY; finite-stage specialization.

proof.text: Depth at least three implies depth at least two. Use canonical depth-two Hartogs restriction [lem-sbc-depth-two-puncture-global-sections] to identify Gamma(W,O_W) with R. Tags 0AVY and 0BK0 identify H^1(W,O_W) with H^2_m(R), which vanishes under depth three.

Put F=O_W. The ascending ideals Ann_R(g^j) stabilize because R is Noetherian. Their restrictions identify with F[g^j], since localization is exact. Choose c which both bounds the stabilization index and annihilates the stabilized torsion sheaf. Form E_j=[F --g^j--> F] in degrees -1,0. Its transition to E_(j-1) is g in degree -1 and the identity in degree 0. The natural map E_j to F/g^j F has cone F[g^j][2]. A sufficiently long transition of these cones is zero. This is the pro-isomorphism explicitly stated in 0H3E.

Apply derived global sections to this pro-isomorphism and then degree-zero cohomology. Zero error transitions stay zero after derived global sections; the long exact sequences show that both the kernels and cokernels of the induced cohomology maps form pro-zero systems (enlarge the bound to accommodate both adjacent connecting maps). Since H^1(W,F)=0, H^0(R Gamma(W,E_j)) is exactly Gamma(W,F)/g^j Gamma(W,F)=R/g^j R, by the triangle for multiplication by g. The induced comparison is the canonical scalar quotient restriction.

The kernel I of R to R/(g) equals (g), and I^j=(g^j). Under the second pullback projection, the structure sheaf on openThickening f W n pushes forward to F/g^(n+1)F. The quotient maps induce the stated transitions. Naturality of GammaSpecIso and the pullback square identify the scalar comparison with GammaSpecIso.inv followed by (openThickeningMap f W n composed with W.ι).appTop.

For fixed n choose m at least n whose kernel transition to n is zero. If a and b have equal scalar restriction at level m, the class of a-b in R/I^(m+1) belongs to this kernel. Its class in R/I^(n+1) is therefore zero, equivalently a-b belongs to I^(n+1). No finite-level injectivity is used. For g=0 or nilpotent g, the eventual constant quotient is R and Hartogs gives the kernel assertion.

proof_origin.place: Finite-stage consequence of the pro-isomorphism in Tag 0H3E, with the depth vanishing of 0AVY and 0BK0.

lean.statement:
theorem punctured_principal_restriction_kernel
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (g : R) (hg : g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
    (hdepth : (3 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := R) R)
    (W : (Spec (.of R)).Opens)
    (hW : ∀ x : Spec (.of R), x ∈ W ↔ x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) :
    let f := Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g})
    let I := RingHom.ker f
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, n ≤ m ∧ ∀ a b : R,
      ((ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv ≫
        (FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickeningMap f W m ≫ W.ι).appTop) a =
      ((ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv ≫
        (FiniteEtale.Adic.openThickeningMap f W m ≫ W.ι).appTop) b →
      a - b ∈ I ^ (n + 1)
